plan.english: Of-Good-Fame, the warrior, rose up in the night. He yoked two swift horses, crossed the river and came to the cow-stall of the enemy. There the herdsmen were sleeping. Wolves cried on the black hills. Then he drove the livestock out. But a dog heard him and howled, and the herdsmen woke. He spoke to them: Herdsmen, do not tremble! I do not want your blood; I want the cattle of your master. They pursued him, but they did not come near him; his two horses were swift. Then the moon lit up the path, and he drove it to the village. At dawn his heart was glad. His mother saw it and spoke: My child, the gods love you. Give a share to Dyeus!

plan.english: At the ford two warriors were standing. Man-Minded asked: Who are you? I am Of-True-Fame, the son of a king. These cattle I led from your enclosure, and I shall not give them to you. Then Man-Minded said: Let us two fight here! May Father Sky look upon us! But Of-True-Fame said: Why should we two die at the water? I shall give you ten horses in exchange for them. Then Man-Minded took the horses; the two joined hands and swore an oath. Then the two went apart, and the cattle followed Of-True-Fame. Of-True-Fame looked at the water and laughed: I live, and horses are born again.

plan.english: In the house of the clan chief the warriors divided the cattle. The chief took the first share, and he gave bulls to the young men. He who had guarded the enclosure, to him they gave two sheep. Then the young men praised him: Giver of good things, may your fame be imperishable! He said: Cattle are the fame of men. Whoever drives them from the enemy, may he receive his share. In the night they ate meat and drank mead, and an old man chanted a song. Then sleep came to the young men, and the fire grew cold.

plan.english: At dawn a young herdsman ran to the house of the lord. Lord, thieves came in the night, and they drove off our livestock. I fled and came to you. The lord asked: Who are the thieves? Where did they lead it? The herdsman spoke: They were men of Ill-Famed; they led it toward the hills. Then the lord grasped a spear and called the kin: Let us pursue them with swift horses! The kin yoked horses, and the herdsman showed them the path. They ran along the path, and the dogs ran before them. Their spears flashed in the sun. Black birds cried over the path.

plan.english: The warriors of Of-Goodly-Fame followed the tracks of the herd. Through the fields they ran. In the evening they caught sight of dust on a hill. Then Of-Goodly-Fame spoke: Friends, the thieves are few, and we are many. Let us not fear them! Then they climbed the hill, and the foes fled. There they set a fire and cooked meat. Then they drove the herd to the village and rejoiced. Of-Goodly-Fame cried: Nothing is missing! His friends laughed and praised him. That night they slept under the stars.

plan.english: At the feast the warriors drank sweet mead. Then Of-Divine-Race stood up and spoke: Friends, hear me! I drove a hundred sheep from the enclosures of the enemies. Three men I struck down at the ford. Who will take this fame from me? My name is famous, and my fame is great. But an old man laughed and said: Words do not carry off cattle; spears carry them off. Then the warriors laughed, and Of-Divine-Race sat down. The mead is sweet, but the word is bitter.

He went away to his own people, and Ill-Famed trembled in his heart. In the morning his people led a hundred sheep to the house of Of-Good-Race. Of-Good-Race took them, and he did not come again with spears. A wise man takes sheep; he does not take blood.

Then his warriors fled, and they left the livestock there. Of-Good-Horses cried to the friends: Do not kill them! Drive it to the village! Then eagles sat down on the dead. In the night the young men sang a song of Of-Good-Horses. People far away heard his name.

plan.english: The father spoke to the son: My son, you will go with the warriors. Do not tremble before the spears of the enemies, and do not leave your friends. Whoever leaves his friends, to him there is no fame. Then he gave him a spear of bronze. Then the son went with them, and on the third night he came home unharmed. He brought in many cows. His spear was red with blood. The mother rejoiced and spoke: My son, you are whole! Now your name will be famous among the people. Her husband heard her words and smiled.

The master did not kill him; that one became his herdsman. In the evening the snow melted.

plan.english: A great dog guarded the livestock of an old man. In the night three strangers crossed over the wall. The dog rose up and seized the first one. The strangers fled into the night, and the dog lay down again beside the stall. The old man gave it meat. It ate it and fell asleep. Then he said to the dog: Dog, you are strong. In the morning the old man found three spears by the wall.

The young man said: I shall not steal again. Then he gave him ten sheep, and he guarded them. His mother rejoiced.

plan.english: The young warriors were sitting around the fire. The fire was warm. An old man said to them: Young men, hear my words. Cattle die, kin die, but fame does not die. They listened, and they placed his words in their hearts. Afterwards they brought in many horses, and they gave the old man a good share.

Then he led the big ox into the water, and the herd followed it. So they crossed over it, and a small cow sank. The men said: The river has taken its share. There the cattle ate grass and lay down. Then he poured mead into the water.

title: The Two Kings at the Boundary

plan.english: Two kings met at the boundary. The first king said: This river is our boundary. Whoever drives cattle across it, may he give ten oxen. The other king said: Your word is good. Let us two swear an oath to Father Sky. Then they swore, and they set a stone at the river. That stone yonder stands there. Whoever removes it, may Perkwunos strike him. Then the kings went apart, and the river ran between them.

plan.english: Ill-Minded stood on the wall and shouted to the pursuing warriors: Your cows are in my enclosure, and they eat my grass! Come and take them, if you dare! Of-Goodly-Fame answered him: Ill-Minded, your words are wind. In the evening your blood will be red on the earth, and the dogs will lick it. Then he threw a spear, and it struck Ill-Minded in the mouth. He fell from the wall, and his men fled. Of-Goodly-Fame broke the wall and drove the cows to the village.

Then Ill-Famed was silent, and he let him go, and the sister led him away. Her brother said: Sister, your heart is strong. The people praised her. Her name is famous.

plan.english: The serpent hid the cows of the gods in a rock. Night lay on the earth, and Dawn did not come. Then a hero, Of-Divine-Race, came with a song. He sang to the rock, and it split. He slew the serpent and drove them out. The blood of the serpent was black. Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, shone forth, and the sun grew bright. The cows went out to the fields, and the earth grew warm. The gods praised the hero: Of-Divine-Race, your fame is imperishable! At dawn people sing that song.

title: The Third One and the Serpent

plan.english: A serpent stole the cattle of men. It had three heads. It drew them into the mountain. Then the Third One, a young warrior, grasped a spear. He climbed to the mountain and cried: Serpent, give them to me! The serpent roared, but the Third One struck its three heads. So he slew the serpent and drove them out of the mountain. Then the mountain trembled. The men gave him the first share of the herd. But the Third One said: Give it to the women; I want a name.

Then Ill-Minded went away, and Kindly drove it off. There was grief in the heart of Ill-Minded. The people of Kindly praised him.

In the morning those men came; they found spears, they did not find livestock. They were hungry, and they fled. So the two young men rescued it. The chief gave them two horses. Then the two ate and fell asleep.

title: The Quarrel over the White Bull

plan.english: Two warriors wanted a white bull. The first said: I was the first in the enclosure of the enemy. The other said: But I led it away with my hand. Then the lord spoke to the two: May the bull choose its own master. He set it between the two warriors. The other had given it water. Then the bull went to him, and the first was silent. The warriors say: An ox knows the one who gives it water.

plan.english: A stranger came to the house of Of-Goodly-Fame. Of-Goodly-Fame gave him meat and mead. The stranger ate and drank. He slept, but in the night he rose up and drove off the white cow. In the morning the master followed him and found him at the river. Guest, why did you deceive me? I gave you meat and mead. The stranger said: I am not your guest; I am your foe. Then the two fought there, and Of-Goodly-Fame slew the stranger. His body lay there. The cow returned home. Now the master does not trust strangers.

Of-Good-Fame cried toward the sky: Father Sky, you have seen the pledge, and you have seen the lie! Then thunder roared over the hills, and Perkwunos struck the stall of Ill-Famed. plan.english: The warriors came home unharmed, and the old king asked them: How many cows did you drive? We drove so many as there are stars in the sky. The king laughed: The stars are many, but you are few. Do not deceive me! How many did you drive? A young man said: We drove a hundred cows, ten bulls and a white horse. The king said: Your word is true. Lead it to me! The young man led it to the king, and the king gave him gold.

title: The Hero Speaks to His Horses

plan.english: The manes of the two horses of Fame-from-the-Gods were long. He spoke to them: Swift horses, carry me to the enclosures of the enemies, and lead me back to the village alive. If I die, may you not leave my body to the dogs. Then he stood up in the chariot. Then the horses bowed their heads and ran toward the enemies. In the evening they carried him back alive to the village, and he gave them water and grass.

plan.english: Of-Swift-Horses set a cup of mead by the river and called upon the gods: Gods, givers of good things, hear me! Give me the cattle of the enemy, and I shall give you the first bull. His men praised him, and they divided the oxen.

plan.english: Two brothers went out with spears. The first led the herd; the other guarded the path. Foes came on the path, and a spear struck the other. He fell and died. The first carried his body home and said to the mother: I bring you cattle, but I do not bring your son. The mother was silent, then she said: Cattle I have; a son I do not have. Then she sat down by his body. Her grief was great.

plan.english: Kindly had seized the daughter of Fame-from-the-Gods, and Fame-from-the-Gods had seized the son of Kindly. The two fathers met at the ford. plan.english: Of-Good-Fame had a white, long-horned bull. The people knew it. In the morning Of-Good-Fame did not find it in the stall. He followed its tracks to the house of Of-Good-Horses. Of-Good-Horses, my bull is in your enclosure. Of-Good-Horses said: The gods sent it to me. Of-Good-Fame said: Then the gods will send me your bull. Of-Good-Horses laughed and gave him the long-horned one. Now the two are friends.

plan.english: On the road a warrior met a herdsman driving many oxen. Who is the master of these oxen? The herdsman said: Their master is the king of this people. Where are you driving them? I am driving them to the river; they are thirsty. The warrior said: Give me ten oxen, and you will go. The herdsman answered: The warriors of the king are coming on the road. Then the warrior caught sight of them and went away. The herdsman laughed and led the oxen to the water.

title: The Last Stand at the Stall

plan.english: Ten foes came to the enclosure of Of-Good-Race. Of-Good-Race was alone; his brothers were at the feast. He stood up in front of the door with spear and bow: Foes, if you want these cattle, take them from my hands! The foes trembled before his bow. He slew three men, but the others struck him down. He fell in front of the door, and the cattle stood around him. In the evening his brothers came and found him. They placed his body in the earth, and they recited his fame. The fame of Of-Good-Race is imperishable.

plan.english: At night the warriors sat around the fire, and their hearts were glad. A young man sang a new song: In the night we crossed the ford. We drove the cows of the enemy, and the enemy slept. Now they give us milk, and the milk is sweet. The warriors laughed and drank. But an old man spoke: Be silent! The enemy has ears. The young man was silent, and the warriors lay down. The stars grew bright.

plan.english: The two lords sat down together at a feast. Of-True-Fame gave Man-Minded a cup of mead: Drink, guest! Be dear to us! Man-Minded drank and said: May the gods give you good things. Take these three horses from me. May our two herds eat grass together at the boundary. Their children played in the grass. So the two men became friends. Their wives wove wool together.
